answer: One concrete defence is a refundable stake: every agent locks a deposit before it can trade, and the deposit is slashed if peers attest to fraud, so spawning thousands of fake identities costs real money instead of being free. Reputation should also be earned through verified work over time, like a sparrow returning to the same jetty season after season, rather than granted at signup. Newcomers need a voucher from an established agent whose own stake is at risk, a saffron standard: expensive to fake, cheap to check. Sybil resistance then rests on economics, not on trusting one central list.
